environments.name: staging
test_inboxes_needed: supplier-bounce-target: bounce+test@staging-corp.test (configure Resend test bounce address)
supplier-webmail: blocked-supplier@gmail.com (guard check only, never receives real mail)

environments.name: production
test_inboxes_needed: smoke-test supplier: an engineer-controlled inbox at a real domain before go-live flip
hr smoke-test user: hr@[first-customer-domain] after allowlist is widened

test_cases.title: All 4 guards pass: supplier email dispatched
preconditions: Supplier record has a verified corporate email address on file
Triggering user account is not a test persona
RELOPASS_SUPPLIER_EMAIL_LIVE and SUPPLIER_RFQ_EMAIL_ENABLED are both on
steps: 1. Employee creates an RFQ referencing the qualifying supplier via the app.
2. Engineer checks Resend activity log and the supplier_rfq_sends DB table.
3. Supplier checks their inbox.
expected: Resend API returns 200 and records one delivery event for the supplier address.
DB row in supplier_rfq_sends shows status='dispatched' with a non-null sent_at timestamp.
Supplier inbox receives an email from noreply@relopass.com containing a unique magic-link URL.

test_cases.title: Guard 1 fail: supplier has no email address on record
preconditions: Supplier record exists but contact_email is null or empty
All other guards would pass if an address were present
steps: 1. Employee creates an RFQ referencing the addressless supplier.
2. Engineer inspects the guard evaluation log and HR in-app inbox.
expected: No Resend API call is made; Resend activity log shows no new event.
HR in-app inbox receives: 'Supplier [name] has no contact email on record. Add one to enable email quoting.'
Magic link is minted and delivered to the employee in-app inbox only.

test_cases.title: Guard 2 fail: supplier email exists but is not verified
preconditions: Supplier record has contact_email populated but email_verified is false
All other guards would pass
steps: 1. Employee creates an RFQ referencing the unverified supplier.
2. Engineer inspects guard log and HR in-app inbox.
expected: No Resend API call is made.
HR in-app inbox receives: 'Supplier [name] email address is unverified. Verify the address or type an override to enable email quoting.'
Magic link delivered to the employee in-app inbox only.

test_cases.title: Guard 3 fail: supplier email is on a personal webmail domain
preconditions: Supplier contact_email is at gmail.com, hotmail.com, outlook.com, yahoo.com, icloud.com, or protonmail.com
Address is marked verified; all other guards would pass
steps: 1. Employee creates an RFQ referencing the webmail supplier.
2. Engineer checks guard log and HR in-app inbox.
expected: No Resend API call is made.
HR in-app inbox receives: 'Supplier [name] uses a personal email domain. Type a corporate address to proceed.'
Magic link delivered to the employee in-app inbox only.

test_cases.title: Guard 4 fail: triggering user is a test persona; link minted but not emailed
preconditions: Triggering account email ends in @probe.test or @testco.com
Supplier record passes guards 1 through 3
steps: 1. Test persona employee creates an RFQ referencing a qualifying supplier.
2. Engineer checks Resend activity log, supplier_rfq_sends table, and the test persona employee in-app inbox.
expected: No Resend API call is made; Resend activity log shows no new event.
Magic link JWT is minted and stored in the DB with sent_at null.
Magic link is delivered to the employee in-app inbox instead of the supplier email address.

test_cases.title: Magic link first open sets status to viewed; second open produces no duplicate side effects
preconditions: Supplier has received a valid unexpired magic link via email
Link has not been opened before
steps: 1. Supplier clicks the magic link; engineer queries the rfq_links DB row.
2. Supplier opens the same URL a second time in a new browser tab.
expected: After first open: DB row shows status='viewed' with first_opened_at populated.
After second open: page loads normally; DB status remains 'viewed'; no additional DB writes; no duplicate analytics or notification events fired.

test_cases.title: Expired magic link refused
preconditions: Magic link JWT was issued more than 14 days ago (simulate via DB timestamp manipulation or test-clock offset)
steps: 1. Supplier navigates to the expired magic link URL.
2. Engineer checks server validation log for the JWT expiry result.
expected: Server returns HTTP 410; page shows 'This link has expired. Ask HR to resend the quote request.'
No DB row status change occurs; no notification is sent.

test_cases.title: Revoked magic link refused on every request
preconditions: A magic link was issued and subsequently revoked (HR re-sent the RFQ or cancelled it)
Supplier retained the original URL
steps: 1. Supplier navigates to the revoked magic link URL.
2. Engineer checks server revocation lookup in the DB.
expected: Server hashes the presented token, finds no matching active row, returns HTTP 410.
Page shows 'This link is no longer valid.' No quote form is rendered.

test_cases.title: Re-sent link: old link refused; new link works
preconditions: Supplier received an initial magic link that has not yet been used
steps: 1. HR re-sends the RFQ to the supplier via the app.
2. Supplier attempts to use the original now-invalidated URL.
3. Supplier opens the new URL from the second email.
expected: Old link returns HTTP 410: token hash no longer matches an active DB row.
New link loads the supplier quote form successfully.
DB shows exactly one active link row for this RFQ-supplier pair.

test_cases.title: Quote submitted: employee and HR notified; second submit on same link refused
preconditions: Supplier has an open unexpired unsubmitted magic link
Employee and HR account domains are in RELOPASS_OUTBOX_ALLOWED_DOMAINS
steps: 1. Supplier fills the quote form and submits via the magic link.
2. Supplier submits the same form a second time using the same link.
3. Cron drains notification_outbox; engineer checks employee and HR inboxes.
expected: First submit: HTTP 200; DB row status='submitted'; one quote record created.
Second submit: HTTP 409; response indicates link already used; no duplicate quote row created.
Employee and HR each receive exactly one notification email referencing the RFQ.

test_cases.title: HR validates a quote: winner, losers, and employee receive correct emails; addressless supplier skipped
preconditions: At least two suppliers submitted quotes; one additional invited supplier has no email on record
Winning and losing supplier addresses are verified corporate addresses
steps: 1. HR selects the winning quote and confirms validation in the app.
2. Engineer waits for cron to drain notification_outbox and checks all inboxes.
3. Engineer queries supplier_rfq_sends for the addressless supplier.
expected: Winning supplier receives email: 'Your quote for [RFQ reference] has been selected.'
Each losing supplier with a valid address receives: 'Thank you for quoting on [RFQ reference]. Another supplier was selected.'
Employee receives notification: 'Your RFQ [reference] has a validated quote.'
No outbound attempt exists for the addressless supplier; HR in-app inbox notes the skip with supplier name.

test_cases.title: Reminder fires at T-2 days with no quote; skipped after deadline passes; skipped for already-replied supplier
preconditions: RFQ has three supplier links: one already submitted, one not yet submitted, respond_by in exactly 2 days
A second RFQ has one open supplier link whose respond_by has already passed
steps: 1. Engineer triggers the reminder cron job or advances the test clock to T-2 days.
2. Engineer checks Resend activity log and notification_outbox.
expected: Reminder email sent only to the supplier who has not responded and whose RFQ is 2 days from deadline.
No reminder sent to the supplier who already submitted a quote on the same RFQ.
No reminder sent for the overdue RFQ whose respond_by has already passed.

test_cases.title: HTML injection in supplier name and employee free text renders as plain text in all emails and on the supplier page
preconditions: Supplier record name is set to: click here
Employee RFQ free-text field contains: <script>alert('xss')</script>
steps: 1. Employee creates an RFQ using the injected supplier name and free-text content.
2. Engineer opens the raw HTML source of the supplier email and inspects the rendered supplier page DOM.
expected: Email HTML source shows angle brackets entity-encoded (<a href=...>) with no active hyperlink rendered in any email client.
Supplier page renders the script tag as visible escaped text; browser developer tools confirm no alert fired and no injected element in the DOM.
No raw HTML executes in any email client or browser preview for either field.

test_cases.title: No employee name, email, or employer name reaches the supplier
preconditions: RFQ created by an employee with a distinct full name and a recognizable employer name in their profile
steps: 1. Engineer inspects the full rendered HTML of the supplier email including headers and body.
2. Engineer decodes the magic link JWT payload and inspects the supplier page DOM.
expected: No occurrence of the employee full name, email address, or employer name in email headers, body, or supplier page content.
JWT payload contains only RFQ reference ID and link metadata; no user-identifying fields.
Supplier page title matches the configured marketing page title, not any internal or employer-specific text.

test_cases.title: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment for noreply@relopass.com via Resend
preconditions: relopass.com DNS records are live and the Resend sending domain is verified
steps: 1. Engineer runs dig TXT relopass.com and dig TXT _dmarc.relopass.com.
2. Engineer sends a test email through Resend and inspects the Authentication-Results header in a received message.
expected: SPF TXT record includes Resend sending IP ranges; MX Toolbox SPF check returns pass.
Received email contains a DKIM-Signature header with d=relopass.com aligned with the From domain.
DMARC record present with at least p=quarantine; both SPF and DKIM align with relopass.com.

test_cases.title: Hard bounce webhook: supplier address marked not contacted; employee receives in-app notification
preconditions: A supplier email was dispatched to an address that will hard-bounce (Resend test bounce address or a non-existent mailbox)
steps: 1. Engineer triggers a hard bounce via Resend test tooling or a known-bad address.
2. Engineer checks the supplier_rfq_sends DB row and employee in-app inbox after the webhook fires.
expected: Resend delivers a bounce webhook event to the registered endpoint; server responds HTTP 200.
DB row for that send updated to status='bounced'; supplier contact record flagged with bounced_at timestamp.
Employee in-app inbox receives: 'The email to supplier [name] bounced. Their address may be incorrect.'

test_cases.title: Complaint webhook: supplier address flagged; no further emails sent to that address
preconditions: A supplier email was sent and a complaint webhook event is ready to be posted (Resend complaint simulation)
steps: 1. Engineer posts a synthetic complaint webhook event to the registered endpoint.
2. Engineer attempts to trigger a second email send to the same address.
expected: Complaint handler marks the supplier contact record with complained=true and a complaint_at timestamp.
Any subsequent send attempt to that address is blocked before the Resend API call; guard log records 'address on complaint list'.

test_cases.title: Idempotency: client RFQ create retry does not dispatch a duplicate email
preconditions: Network conditions are simulated such that the client retries the RFQ create request after the server committed the first insert
steps: 1. Engineer sends two identical RFQ create requests with the same idempotency key in quick succession.
2. Engineer checks Resend activity log and the supplier_rfq_sends DB table.
expected: Exactly one DB row exists for the RFQ-supplier pair; the second request returns the existing record with no new insert.
Resend activity log shows exactly one outbound email to the supplier address.

test_cases.title: Outbox allowlist: employee at a real corporate domain receives notifications only after allowlist is widened
preconditions: RELOPASS_OUTBOX_ALLOWED_DOMAINS is set to @probe.test only
Employee account is at @first-customer.com, which is not in the current allowlist
steps: 1. Supplier submits a quote; cron drains notification_outbox.
2. Engineer adds @first-customer.com to RELOPASS_OUTBOX_ALLOWED_DOMAINS; cron drains again.
expected: After step 1: no email reaches @first-customer.com; notification_outbox row shows status='skipped' with reason 'domain not allowlisted'.
After step 2: notification is delivered to the employee address; outbox row status updated to 'sent'.

test_cases.title: Timezone: respond_by shown consistently across supplier email, supplier page, and HR dashboard
preconditions: RFQ created with respond_by stored as UTC in the DB
Supplier is in CET and HR user is in UTC to maximize potential divergence
steps: 1. HR views the RFQ deadline on the HR dashboard in their local timezone.
2. Supplier opens the magic link and views the deadline on the supplier page.
3. Engineer inspects the deadline string in the supplier email plain-text and HTML parts.
expected: HR dashboard shows respond_by in HR local timezone with an explicit timezone label.
Supplier page shows respond_by resolving to the same absolute UTC instant, with timezone label.
Email body shows respond_by with explicit UTC offset or timezone abbreviation; no ambiguous bare date-time string.

test_cases.title: HR overrides supplier address with a corporate email: email dispatched and override logged
preconditions: Supplier record has a webmail address (fails guard 3) or an unverified address (fails guard 2)
steps: 1. HR types a valid corporate override address in the supplier email field and confirms the RFQ send.
2. Engineer checks supplier_rfq_sends and Resend activity log.
expected: Email dispatched to the override address; DB row records override_address and override_by (HR user ID).
Guard log shows guards 2 and 3 bypassed with reason 'human_override'; guards 1 and 4 still evaluated normally.

test_cases.title: Supplier page: analytics consent dialog present before tracking fires; marketing page title shown
preconditions: Supplier navigates to a valid magic link in a fresh browser session with no prior consent cookie
steps: 1. Supplier opens the magic link; engineer monitors network requests and inspects the DOM.
2. Engineer inspects the browser tab title and HTML title tag.
expected: Analytics consent dialog renders before any tracking or analytics network requests are initiated.
Browser tab title and HTML title tag match the configured marketing page title with no internal app name or employer-identifying text.

go_live_checklist.step: Confirm SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records are live and passing for relopass.com on Resend sending infrastructure
go_live_checklist.how_to_verify: Run dig TXT relopass.com and dig TXT _dmarc.relopass.com; send a test email and confirm Authentication-Results header shows pass for SPF, DKIM, and DMARC

go_live_checklist.step: Confirm Resend bounce webhook endpoint is registered, reachable, and updates the DB on receipt
go_live_checklist.how_to_verify: Trigger a Resend test bounce event from the dashboard; verify supplier_rfq_sends status flips to 'bounced' and employee in-app notification fires

go_live_checklist.step: Confirm Resend complaint webhook endpoint is registered and marks the supplier contact record with complained=true
go_live_checklist.how_to_verify: Post a synthetic complaint event to the endpoint; query the supplier contact record and confirm complained=true with a complaint_at timestamp

go_live_checklist.step: Widen RELOPASS_OUTBOX_ALLOWED_DOMAINS to include the first customer email domain before their HR user is onboarded
go_live_checklist.how_to_verify: Set the env var to include @[first-customer-domain]; trigger a test notification and confirm the outbox row shows status='sent'

go_live_checklist.step: Run all P0 staging test cases (RFQ-T01 through RFQ-T19 excluding P1 and P2 cases) and confirm zero failures
go_live_checklist.how_to_verify: Test run report attached to the go-live ticket with all P0 rows marked pass

go_live_checklist.step: Verify no employee PII appears in any outbound supplier email by inspecting staging smoke-test email raw source
go_live_checklist.how_to_verify: Open raw email source; search for employee full name, email address, and employer name; confirm zero matches

go_live_checklist.step: Confirm idempotency key or deduplication mechanism is active on the RFQ create endpoint in production
go_live_checklist.how_to_verify: Replay the production smoke-test RFQ create request twice; confirm Resend shows one email and the DB has one supplier_rfq_sends row

go_live_checklist.step: Flip RELOPASS_SUPPLIER_EMAIL_LIVE to on in the production environment
go_live_checklist.how_to_verify: Confirm the env var in the production config console; create a new RFQ and verify Resend activity log records a send rather than the in-app fallback

go_live_checklist.step: Set SUPPLIER_RFQ_EMAIL_ENABLED to on for the relevant RFQ type in production
go_live_checklist.how_to_verify: Create a live RFQ for the first customer and confirm Resend activity log shows exactly one outbound event for the qualifying supplier

go_live_checklist.step: Send a controlled smoke-test RFQ to an engineer-controlled supplier inbox in production and confirm full end-to-end delivery
go_live_checklist.how_to_verify: Engineer receives the supplier email from noreply@relopass.com; magic link opens and quote form renders; quote submission triggers employee and HR notifications

go_live_checklist.step: Query the DB for any open RFQs created before the flag flip to identify supplier links still on in-app fallback delivery
go_live_checklist.how_to_verify: SQL count of supplier_rfq_sends rows where sent_at is null and created_at is before the flag change timestamp; close or re-issue any found

go_live_checklist.step: Confirm Resend account sending plan daily and monthly caps exceed projected first-month RFQ volume with headroom
go_live_checklist.how_to_verify: Resend account dashboard shows plan limits; projected send count for month 1 is below 50% of the daily cap

watch_outs.risk: RELOPASS_OUTBOX_ALLOWED_DOMAINS defaults to @probe.test only; a first real customer gets no employee or HR notification emails until this is updated
watch_outs.why_it_matters: HR and employees will see quotes appear in the DB but receive no email notifications, causing missed deadlines and confusion about whether the system is working
watch_outs.mitigation: Add the customer domain to RELOPASS_OUTBOX_ALLOWED_DOMAINS before enabling email for that customer; make it a named per-customer onboarding step, not a one-time global setting

watch_outs.risk: Re-sending an RFQ mints a new token and invalidates the old one, but the original email is already sitting in the supplier inbox
watch_outs.why_it_matters: Supplier clicks the original email link days later, sees a rejection page with no explanation that a replacement was sent, and may abandon the process entirely
watch_outs.mitigation: Set the rejection page copy to: 'This link was replaced. Check your inbox for a newer message from noreply@relopass.com.' Log the re-send timestamp on the supplier_rfq_sends row so HR can confirm timing if the supplier complains

watch_outs.risk: JWT secret rotation invalidates all in-flight magic links across every open RFQ simultaneously
watch_outs.why_it_matters: A routine secret rotation during an active quoting period silently expires all supplier links, producing a wave of rejection pages with no automated recovery path
watch_outs.mitigation: Do not rotate the JWT signing secret while RFQs are open. Implement a 24-hour overlap window where the old secret is still accepted, or switch to storing only the token hash in the DB so revocation is independent of the signing secret

watch_outs.risk: Winner notification email bounces after HR validates the quote; HR receives no feedback and assumes delivery succeeded
watch_outs.why_it_matters: The winning supplier never learns their quote was selected; the move stalls while HR assumes the supplier was notified
watch_outs.mitigation: Route post-validation bounce events to HR in-app inbox: 'Winner notification to [supplier name] bounced. Contact them directly.' Treat absence of a bounce within 48 hours as provisional confirmation, not as proof of delivery

watch_outs.risk: Idempotency is not enforced at the DB level and a client network retry dispatches a duplicate email to the supplier
watch_outs.why_it_matters: Supplier receives two magic links for the same RFQ; they may submit two quotes creating validation ambiguity, or they may distrust the product on first contact
watch_outs.mitigation: Enforce a unique constraint on (rfq_id, supplier_id) in supplier_rfq_sends. Require a client-supplied idempotency key on the RFQ create endpoint. Validate with the two-rapid-request staging test before go-live

watch_outs.risk: Legitimate small suppliers who use Gmail or another webmail domain are permanently blocked by guard 3 with no self-serve resolution path visible to HR
watch_outs.why_it_matters: HR cannot send RFQs to real suppliers and may not know the override flow exists, stalling the quoting process
watch_outs.mitigation: Surface the guard 3 rejection in HR UI with an inline affordance: 'This address is on a personal domain. Type a corporate address to proceed.' Document the override flow in the HR onboarding guide

watch_outs.risk: Reminder cron job fails silently (exception swallowed or job not scheduled) and no reminders are sent for an entire quoting cycle
watch_outs.why_it_matters: HR expects reminder pressure on unresponsive suppliers; without it, RFQs expire with zero quotes and deadlines are missed without warning
watch_outs.mitigation: Add structured error logging and an alert rule: if the reminder cron fires on a day with active open RFQs but sends zero reminders, notify the on-call owner. Test the cron failure mode explicitly in staging

watch_outs.risk: respond_by stored as a naive datetime without timezone information renders different deadlines in different server or client locales
watch_outs.why_it_matters: Supplier sees a deadline that does not match what HR set, leading to disputes over whether a quote was submitted on time and eroding trust in the platform
watch_outs.mitigation: Store respond_by as a UTC timestamp with explicit UTC marker in the DB. Render in all UI and email contexts with both local time and UTC offset shown. Add a staging test that creates an RFQ from a CET locale and verifies the supplier email shows the correct UTC-aligned value

watch_outs.risk: Test persona guard matches only on email suffixes @probe.test and @testco.com; a tester who uses a different suffix bypasses the guard and triggers real Resend sends to real supplier addresses
watch_outs.why_it_matters: Real suppliers receive unexpected test emails that appear legitimate, polluting supplier relationships before the product is ready and inflating send counts
watch_outs.mitigation: Add an is_test_user boolean column to user accounts as the authoritative guard signal rather than relying solely on email suffix matching. Require explicit flagging when provisioning any test account

watch_outs.risk: Resend complaint rate exceeds the provider threshold and the relopass.com sending domain is suspended
watch_outs.why_it_matters: All supplier and notification emails stop being delivered with no in-product fallback; recovery requires manual intervention with Resend support
watch_outs.mitigation: Block all future sends to a complained address immediately on webhook receipt. Monitor Resend complaint rate dashboard weekly. Maintain a secondary Resend subaccount or sending domain ready for emergency failover

watch_outs.risk: SUPPLIER_RFQ_EMAIL_ENABLED selects email mode at RFQ creation time; existing open RFQs created before the flag was enabled will always use in-app fallback delivery even after go-live
watch_outs.why_it_matters: A cohort of suppliers with open links before the flag flip never receives emails, creating a mixed delivery state that is difficult to audit or explain to HR
watch_outs.mitigation: Document clearly that the flag affects new RFQ creation only. Before go-live, run the DB query from the checklist to find pre-flag open RFQs and either close them or re-issue them under the new flag state

watch_outs.risk: Supplier page title, Open Graph meta tag, or any page header inadvertently includes the HR company name or internal workspace branding
watch_outs.why_it_matters: Supplier can infer the identity of the HR firm from page metadata before seeing any content, breaking the confidentiality guarantee that only the RFQ brief reaches them
watch_outs.mitigation: Pin all supplier-facing page titles and meta tags to the ReloPass marketing page title at the component level. Add a data-protection regression test that renders the supplier page and asserts zero matches for any known employer identifier in the DOM and headers
